definition: Curriculum development is the process of designing or improving an educational program by deciding what content will be taught, how it will be taught and assessed, and how it will be implemented in a specific setting. It is informed by evidence about learner needs, contextual influences, and barriers or supports to putting the curriculum into practice.

reasons: The definition adds unsupported generalizations not stated in the packet, including that curriculum development is specifically a process of “designing or improving” an educational program and that it is informed by evidence about learner needs.

The packet supports curriculum-related elements such as curricular content, teaching methods, assessment strategies, and contextual influences on implementation, but it does not define curriculum development itself or establish the broader abstract definition given.

The provided definition makes broad, general claims about “curriculum development” (e.g., deciding content, teaching, assessment, implementation; being informed by evidence about learner needs and contextual barriers/supports), but the source packet only describes a telemedicine education scoping review protocol and does not supply or support a definition of “curriculum development” with these elements.

The packet mentions “curriculum development” only as an anticipated outcome (“inform future curriculum development”) in relation to telemedicine training; it does not define the term or specify the meaning in the way the definition does.

No substantive support is provided in the packet for the specific phrasing/sense of “curriculum development” used in the definition (design/improve educational program; informed by evidence about learner needs and implementation barriers/supports).
